name: W adds states
summary: Merging the states |0⟩+a|1⟩ and |0⟩+b|1⟩ with a W-spider gives |0⟩+(a+b)|1⟩.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. Read as a merge (dot on the right) it maps $|00\rangle\mapsto|0\rangle$, $|01\rangle, |10\rangle\mapsto|1\rangle$ and $|11\rangle\mapsto 0$.

A one-legged Z-box with label $a$ is the state $|0\rangle + a|1\rangle$ (the same as a one-legged H-box with label $a$). Merging two such states with a W-spider drops the $|11\rangle$ term and adds the labels: the W-spider implements addition. This is the basis of the encoding of arithmetic in the GHZ/W- and ZW-calculi, and of the 'Add' gadget used to build sums of diagrams.
parameter_notes: Shown for two states; holds for any number of states merged by one W-spider.
